req.title: DELETE is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 on second and subsequent DELETE calls for the same playerId.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-030 requires DELETE /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} to be idempotent: the first call returns HTTP 204, and every subsequent call for the same squad number returns HTTP 404. The test suite covers: (1) positive — first DELETE returns 204, second DELETE returns 404 (STC: exists→deleted→not-found); (2) negative — DELETE on a squad number that never existed returns 404 immediately (NEG); (3) boundary — DELETE on the lowest squad number in the fixture (1) then re-DELETE returns 404 (BVA); (4) additional state-transition — three consecutive DELETEs all return 404 after the first (STC); (5) decision-table — verifying exact status codes for both the 204 and 404 branches to kill comparison-operator mutations (DT). All tests use the in-process FastAPI TestClient, reference only fixture squad numbers, and assert exact HTTP status codes.

tests.name: test_delete_idempotent_first_204_second_404
preconditions: Player with squad_number=10 (Messi) exists in the database
expected: First DELETE returns HTTP 204 No Content
Second DELETE returns HTTP 404 Not Found
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_idempotent_first_204_second_404():
    r1 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/10')
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    r2 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/10')
    assert r2.status_code == 404

tests.name: test_delete_first_call_not_404_and_second_call_not_204
preconditions: Player with squad_number=7 (de Paul) exists in the database
actions: Assert response status is exactly 204 (not 404, not 200, not 500)
Assert response status is exactly 404 (not 204, not 200, not 500)
expected: First DELETE is NOT 404 — it is exactly 204
Second DELETE is NOT 204 — it is exactly 404
trace: R-PLAYER-030: decision table — both branches of the exists/not-exists check
DT: catches mutations that swap 204<->404 or flip the existence check
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_first_call_not_404_and_second_call_not_204():
    r1 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/7')
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    assert r1.status_code != 404
    assert r1.status_code != 200
    assert r1.status_code != 500
    r2 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/7')
    assert r2.status_code == 404
    assert r2.status_code != 204
    assert r2.status_code != 200
    assert r2.status_code != 500

tests.name: test_delete_idempotent_player_gone_confirmed_by_get
preconditions: Player with squad_number=20 (Mac Allister) exists in the database
actions: Send GET /players/squadnumber/20 to confirm player exists (expect 200)
Send GET /players/squadnumber/20 to confirm player is gone (expect 404)
trace: R-PLAYER-030: full state-transition verification including GET confirmation
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_idempotent_player_gone_confirmed_by_get():
    rg1 = client.get('/players/squadnumber/20')
    assert rg1.status_code == 200
    rd1 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/20')
    assert rd1.status_code == 204
    rg2 = client.get('/players/squadnumber/20')
    assert rg2.status_code == 404
    rd2 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/20')
    assert rd2.status_code == 404
